item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees tuvieron una sólida temporada regular pese a las lesiones de jugadores clave como Aaron Judge.
Aun así, se clasificaron a los playoffs de la MLB de 2026.
El desempeño de Cody Bellinger fue una de las claves de ese éxito.
Fue el mejor jugador defensivo del equipo.
La esposa de una querida estrella de los Yankees le dedica un emotivo mensaje
Esta semana se supo que Bellinger ganó un prestigioso premio.
La MLB escribió el 6 de noviembre: “Cody Bellinger suma el Rawlings Platinum Glove a su vitrina llena de trofeos 🏆 Se une a Jose Trevino (2022) como los únicos jugadores de los Yankees que han ganado el Platinum Glove en los 16 años de historia del premio”.
Su esposa, Chase, publicó entonces un emotivo mensaje en Instagram.
Escribió: “¡¡Señor Platino!!”
Los comentarios en su publicación
Cody Bellinger, número 35 de los New York Yankees, celebra con su esposa, Chase Carter Bellinger, tras ganar el premio Ted Williams al Jugador Más Valioso en el Juego de Estrellas de la MLB de 2026, disputado en Citizens Bank Park el 14 de julio de 2026 en Filadelfia, Pensilvania.
Esto fue lo que escribieron en los comentarios de su publicación:
Ashley Rodón: “Dos de las mejores personas en una sola foto 🥹 ¡¡¡¡Se ganó ese título con creces!!!!”
Natalie McMahon: “¡¡¡Ufff!!!”
Madisyn Seager: “Me encanta todo esto”
Cody Bellinger, número 35 de los New York Yankees, reacciona tras conectar un jonrón de 2 carreras en la cuarta entrada del primer partido de una doble cartelera ante los Tampa Bay Rays, disputado en Yankee Stadium el 22 de septiembre de 2026 en el Bronx, Nueva York.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees had a strong regular season despite injuries to key players such as Aaron Judge.
They were still able to get into the 2026 MLB playoffs.
One of the reasons for their success was the play of Cody Bellinger.
He was the team’s best fielder.
Wife Of Beloved Yankees Star Sends Out Heartfelt Post
This week, news came out that Bellinger won a big time award.
MLB wrote (on November 6): “Cody Bellinger adds the Rawlings Platinum Glove to his crowded trophy case 🏆 He joins Jose Trevino (2022) as the only Yankees to win the Platinum Glove in the 16-year history of the award.”
Bellinger’s wife (Chase) then made a heartfelt post to Instagram.
She wrote: “Mr Platinum!!”
Comments On Her Post
Cody Bellinger #35 of the New York Yankees celebrates his wife, Chase Carter Bellinger after winning the Ted Williams Most Valuable Player Award at the 2026 MLB All-Star Game at Citizens Bank Park on July 14, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Here’s what people were saying in the comments of her post:
Ashley Rodón: “Two of the best people in one pic 🥹 Earned every bit of that title!!!!”
Natalie McMahon: “sheeeesh!!”
Madisyn Seager: “Love everything about this”
Cody Bellinger #35 of the New York Yankees reacts to hitting a 2-run home run in the fourth inning during game one of a doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on September 22, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
@avaaoconnor: “STUNNING lady 💃💃💃”
@landin.murphy: “Omgggggggg chase 🔥🔥🔥
oh & congrats Cody !!!!”
Looking At Bellinger
Cody Bellinger #35 of the New York Yankees reacts after a ground out against the Boston Red Sox during the third inning in game two of the American League Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on September 30, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. 
Bellinger was picked in the 4th round of the 2013 MLB Draft.
He spent the first six years of his career playing for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
In 2019, Bellinger won the National League MVP Award (and then won a title in 2020).
Cody Bellinger #35 of the New York Yankees looks on from the dugout before the game against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Yankee Stadium on April 01, 2025 in the Bronx borough of New York City.
Bellinger then had a two-year stop with the Chicago Cubs (before the Yankees).

item.content:encoded:
AP
CINCINNATI (AP) — Jose Trevino lined a two-run single to right field with the bases loaded in the sixth inning and the Cincinnati Reds rallied for a 6-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs on Friday night.
Michael Conforto had three hits for the Cubs, who are tied with the Padres and Phillies at 85-69 for the three National League wild cards — five games ahead of Arizona with eight to play.
Chicago had the potential tying run at the plate with two outs in the ninth when Michael Busch was caught stealing second base by Trevino on a pitchout.
Clay Holmes (6-8) went 5 1/3 innings for the Cubs and allowed six runs.
Eugenio Suárez tied it at 4 with a base hit to drive in Elly De La Cruz. Héctor Rodríguez grounded into a fielder's choice as Tyler Stephenson was called out at home before Trevino came through with the go-ahead hit.
De La Cruz also drove in two runs for the Reds, who dropped three of four to the Los Angeles Dodgers in their previous series.
Ian Happ homered in the third to tie it at 2 and Seiya Suzuki had a two-run single with the bases loaded in the fourth to put the Cubs up 4-3.
Julian Aguiar (2-1) got the win in relief, allowing two runs in three innings. All-Star starter Chase Burns, who is on an innings restriction, gave up two runs in three innings.
A matchup of left-handers on Saturday. Matthew Boyd (8-5, 4.16 ERA) takes the mound for Chicago while Nick Lodolo (3-5, 5.12) goes for Cincinnati.
___
This story has been corrected to show that Trevino’s two-run single came in the sixth inning, not the seventh.
